newly_discovered_entity_names: HPV → CERVICAL INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA (CIN): HPV INFECTION CAUSES ABNORMAL CERVICAL CELL CHANGES KNOWN AS CIN OR CERVICAL DYSPLASIA.
HPV → HPV VACCINATION: THE HPV VACCINE PREVENTS NEW HPV INFECTIONS.

STAGE 1B1 CERVICAL CANCER IS LARGER THAN 5 MM BUT SMALLER THAN 2 CM. STAGE 1B2 AND 1B3 CERVICAL CANCER IS ONLY IN THE CERVIX; IN STAGE 1B2, THE CANCER IS BETWEEN 2 AND 4 CM, AND IN STAGE 1B3, THE CANCER IS LARGER THAN 4 CM. STAGE 2 CERVICAL CANCER HAS GROWN BEYOND THE CERVIX. IF THE CANCER HAS GROWN INTO THE UPPER VAGINA, THE STAGE IS 2A. STAGE 2A1 CANCERS ARE 4 CM OR SMALLER; STAGE 2A2 CANCERS ARE LARGER THAN 4 CM. STAGE 2B CANCER HAS GROWN INTO THE PARAMETRIUM. STAGE 3A CERVICAL CANCER HAS GROWN INTO THE LOWER THIRD OF THE VAGINA. STAGE 3B CERVICAL CANCER HAS GROWN INTO THE PELVIC WALL AND/OR HAS CAUSED KIDNEY SWELLING OR DYSFUNCTION. STAGE 3C CERVICAL CANCER HAS CANCER IN LYMPH NODES NEAR THE CERVIX (PELVIC LYMPH NODES) AND/OR IN LYMPH NODES IN THE ABDOMEN (PARA-AORTIC LYMPH NODES). STAGE 4A CERVICAL CANCER HAS SPREAD TO NEARBY ORGANS, SUCH AS THE BLADDER OR RECTUM. STAGE 4B CERVICAL CANCER IS METASTATIC, HAVING SPREAD TO THE LIVER, LUNGS, ABDOMEN, BONE, OR OTHER DISTANT SITES OR LYMPH NODES [DATA: SOURCES (172); ENTITIES (1033, 1034, 1035, 953)].
CERVICAL CANCER → CERVICAL INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA (CIN): CERVICAL CANCER STARTS AS CIN, AREAS OF ABNORMAL PRE-CANCEROUS CELLS ON THE CERVIX.

RISK FACTORS THAT INCREASE SUSCEPTIBILITY INCLUDE IMMUNOSUPPRESSION (SUCH AS FROM HIV/AIDS), SMOKING, HIGH PARITY, ORAL CONTRACEPTIVE USE, EARLY SEXUAL ACTIVITY, MULTIPLE SEXUAL PARTNERS, AND HISTORY OF SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS. AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL, DNA MUTATIONS IN CERVICAL CELLS MAKE THEM ABNORMAL, LEADING TO MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION. THE DISEASE IS STAGED USING THE FIGO SYSTEM, AND TREATMENT IS TAILORED TO THE STAGE AND INDIVIDUAL PATIENT CIRCUMSTANCES [DATA: ENTITIES (585, 918, 921, 916, 927, 928, 915, 959); RELATIONSHIPS (2250, 2252, 2258, 2261); SOURCES (169, 172)].
OTHER HPV TYPES CAN CAUSE ABNORMAL SKIN GROWTHS, CALLED WARTS, TO FORM ON THE ANUS, GENITALS, OR OTHER AREAS OF THE BODY [DATA: SOURCES (169)].
